_readme: The app's changelog, as the repository states it. This file is the source
of truth for everything the Updates side of the in-app bell shows.
WHAT GOES IN HERE
A change a household would actually notice. This is a changelog, not a
commit log — it is read by the people living in the house, and the bar is
"would somebody notice this without being told, and be glad they were?"
Yes: a new screen or capability; a change to how something already works
that people have to relearn; a fix for something people knew was broken;
anything that changes what the app costs, asks for or keeps.
No: refactors, renames, tests, dependency bumps, schema and index work, a
padding tweak, a colour, a performance win nobody could feel, a bug fixed
before anybody hit it. Not secrets — just not news. A changelog padded
with them is one people stop opening, which costs the entries that mattered.
One entry per release, not per commit. Six bullets under one headline beat
six headlines; that is what `highlights` is for. Write it for the
household, never for the repository.
Edit it in the SAME COMMIT as the work it describes, then:
cd backend && npx convex run inbox:syncChangelog "$(cat changelog.json)"
Idempotent by `slug`, so running it on every deploy is the intent. An entry
already published keeps its publication date — fixing a typo in an old note
does not move it to the top of everybody's feed or light the badge again.
FIELDS
slug       required, stable, unique. Convention: "<version>-<short-name>".
Changing it files a second entry; never change one after it
has shipped.
version    the app version this ships in. THIS IS A GATE, not a label:
a client on 1.8.1 draws a 1.9.0 entry as "coming soon" rather
than promising a button it does not have. Omit for an
announcement that is true on every build.
kind       feature | improvement | fix | announcement
title      one line, sentence case, no trailing full stop.
body       a short paragraph. What changed and why it is better.
highlights optional bullets. Up to 12, each one short enough to read at a
glance.
translations optional. The same note in the app's other languages:
[{ "language": "tr", "title": ..., "body": ..., "highlights": [...] }]
The fields above are the BASE TEXT AND THE FALLBACK, in English.
A note with no Turkish reads in English rather than reading as
nothing. A half-written one (title but no body) is dropped, so
the reader gets the complete English note instead of a heading
over empty space.
pinned     optional. Floats to the top until unpinned.
draft      optional. true keeps it out of the feed entirely.
Newest entries go at the TOP of `entries` — the file reads like the feed.

entries.title: No more crash when you close a note on a house problem
entries.body: Closing a status note, a parts list or a visit on a house problem could crash the app. Fixed. Big thanks to @goksu.ozahishali for catching it on TestFlight!
highlights: Notes, parts and visit sheets close like they should
Shout-out to @goksu.ozahishali for the crash report

translations.title: Ev sorunlarında notu kapatınca uygulama artık çökmüyor
translations.body: Bir ev sorununda notu, parça listesini ya da usta ziyaretini kapatınca uygulama çöküyordu. Hallettik. TestFlight'tan haber verdiği için @goksu.ozahishali'ya çok teşekkürler!
highlights: Not, parça ve ziyaret ekranları artık düzgün kapanıyor
Çökmeyi yakaladığın için sağ ol @goksu.ozahishali

entries.title: Past events, and what they came to
entries.body: Once an event is over, opening it shows how it went — what it cost against the budget, who said they were coming, what got bought and what was on the menu — instead of a plan you could still change. The calendar has a new Past events page too: a year of what the house did, with the spending on each and in total.
highlights: A finished event can't be moved, re-planned or stocked up for by accident
You can still log a receipt that turns up after the party
Leftover shopping for an event that's over comes off the list in one tap
Editing a repeating event no longer wipes its earlier dates

translations.title: Geçmiş etkinlikler ve neye mal oldukları
translations.body: Bir etkinlik bittiğinde, açtığınızda hâlâ değiştirilebilen bir plan yerine nasıl geçtiğini görürsünüz: bütçeye göre ne kadar tuttuğu, kimlerin geleceğini söylediği, neyin alındığı ve menüde ne olduğu. Takvimde yeni bir Geçmiş etkinlikler sayfası da var: evin bir yıl boyunca yaptıkları, her birinin ve toplamın harcamasıyla.
highlights: Bitmiş bir etkinlik yanlışlıkla taşınamaz, yeniden planlanamaz, alışverişi yapılamaz
Partiden sonra gelen bir fişi yine de ekleyebilirsiniz
Bitmiş bir etkinlikten kalan alışveriş tek dokunuşla listeden çıkar
Tekrarlanan bir etkinliği düzenlemek artık önceki tarihlerini silmiyor

entries.title: The notifications panel opens again, and speaks Turkish
entries.body: Opening the bell showed an error instead of the household's activity. It does not any more. Release notes are also translated now, so the Updates tab reads in whichever language the app is set to rather than always in English.
highlights: Tapping the bell no longer shows an error
Update notes now follow the app's language

translations.title: Bildirimler paneli yeniden açılıyor, üstelik Türkçe konuşuyor
translations.body: Zile dokununca evin hareketleri yerine bir hata görünüyordu; artık görünmüyor. Sürüm notları da çevrildi: Güncellemeler sekmesi her zaman İngilizce olmak yerine uygulamanın diline göre okunuyor.
highlights: Zile dokunmak artık hata vermiyor
Sürüm notları uygulamanın dilini takip ediyor

entries.title: Notifications and updates, in one place
entries.body: Every notification your household has ever sent now stays put. Tap the bell on the Home tab to scroll back through what everyone has been doing, filter it by what you care about, and read what has changed in the app itself — two feeds, one button.
highlights: Nothing is lost to a swiped-away banner any more
Filter the household feed by chores, money, shopping and the rest
A separate changelog, so app news never buries a leaking tap
Your own actions never light the badge

translations.title: Bildirimler ve güncellemeler, tek bir yerde
translations.body: Evinizde gönderilen her bildirim artık kayboluyor değil. Ana sayfadaki zile dokunun; herkesin neler yaptığını geriye doğru okuyun, ilgilendiğiniz konulara göre süzün ve uygulamanın kendisinde nelerin değiştiğini görün — iki akış, tek bir düğme.
highlights: Kaydırıp geçtiğiniz bir bildirim artık kaybolmuyor
Ev akışını işlere, paraya, alışverişe ve diğerlerine göre süzün
Ayrı bir sürüm notu akışı; uygulama haberleri akan bir musluğu gömmüyor
Kendi yaptıklarınız rozeti hiç yakmıyor
